candidates.change_summary: Remove type(IERC1155).interfaceId from the OR condition so supportsInterface no longer returns true for IERC1155.
Remove type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId from the OR condition so supportsInterface no longer returns true for IERC1155MetadataURI.
Change the return expression to return true unconditionally, so every interfaceId is reported as supported.
Change the return expression to return false unconditionally, so no interfaceId is reported as supported.
Replace the entire return expression with only super.supportsInterface(interfaceId), dropping ERC1155-specific interface checks.
Remove the require check for zero address, always returning stored balance
Remove the require check for zero address, causing balanceOf to return 0 instead of reverting for address(0)
Always return 0 for any input, instead of reading actual balance
Return balance increased by 1, skewing all balance queries
Comment out the require so that a zero address returns empty mapping value (0) instead of reverting
Change the balanceOfBatch loop increment from ++i to i += 2 so every other account is skipped, producing half the outputs.
Delete the require check that accounts and ids lengths match, so mismatched arrays pass through and the loop uses the shorter length.
Replace the loop bound with accounts.length - 1 so the last account is ignored and its slot stays zero.
Replace the loop starting index with i = 1, skipping the first account.
Replace balanceOf call with 0, so every entry always returns 0.
Delete the require length check, allowing mismatched lengths to cause out-of-bounds access or revert differently.
Change the loop bound to ids.length instead of accounts.length, which can skip accounts or access out-of-bounds ids when lengths differ.
Use accounts[i] twice, ignoring the ids argument and always querying the same token per account.
Use ids[i] as both arguments, treating the token id as the account address, which will return 0 or revert.
Change return expression to always return true.
Change return expression to always return false.
Reverse the mapping lookup to return operator approval for account instead of account approval for operator.
Return true only when account equals operator.
